learningObjectives.title: Types of software (system and application software)

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of system software?
options: Operating system
Spreadsheet software
Word processor
Web browser
questions.explain: An operating system is system software that manages the computer's hardware and provides a platform for application software to run.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of application software?
options: Word processor
Device driver
Operating system
Linker
questions.explain: A word processor is application software because it lets the user carry out a specific task, whereas the others are system software.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a device driver?
options: To allow the operating system to communicate with a piece of hardware
To translate high-level code into machine code
To edit and enhance digital photographs
To create automatic backups of user files
questions.explain: A device driver contains the instructions needed for the operating system to communicate with and control a specific hardware device.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a task carried out by an operating system?
options: Writing a business letter
Managing memory
Managing files
Managing input and output devices
questions.explain: Writing a letter is done using application software; managing memory, files and devices are all operating system tasks.

questions.q: A company buys a new computer that needs software to manage its hardware, control memory and provide a platform for other programs to run. Which type of software is needed?
options: An operating system
A spreadsheet package
A photo-editing application
A web browser
questions.explain: Managing hardware and memory and providing a platform for other programs are the defining roles of an operating system.

questions.q: What is an interrupt?
options: A signal sent to the processor that may cause a break in the execution of the current routine
A permanent shutdown of the computer system
A type of application software
A programming error that cannot be corrected
questions.explain: An interrupt is a signal sent to the processor by a device or program that may pause the currently running routine so it can be dealt with.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a hardware interrupt?
options: A printer running out of paper
A division by zero in a program
An arithmetic overflow error
Two processes trying to access the same memory in a program
questions.explain: A printer running out of paper is generated by a hardware device, making it a hardware interrupt.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a software interrupt?
options: An attempt to divide a number by zero
A paper jam in the printer
A key being pressed on the keyboard
A disk drive failing to respond
questions.explain: A division-by-zero error is caused by a running program, making it a software interrupt.

questions.q: What does the processor do when it receives and accepts an interrupt?
options: It saves the state of the current task and runs an interrupt service routine
It immediately shuts the computer down
It permanently deletes the running program
It ignores the signal until the program finishes
questions.explain: The processor saves its current state, services the interrupt using an interrupt service routine, then restores the state and resumes.

questions.q: A user presses a key on the keyboard while a document is being printed. What is generated so the processor can respond to the key press?
options: An interrupt
A compiler
A device driver
A translator
questions.explain: The key press sends an interrupt signal to the processor so it can pause its current work and handle the input.

questions.q: Which of the following is a low-level language?
options: Assembly language
Python
Java
Visual Basic
questions.explain: Assembly language is a low-level language that is closely related to the processor's machine code, unlike the high-level languages listed.

questions.q: Assembly language instructions are written using:
options: Mnemonics
Binary digits only
Full English sentences
Hexadecimal colour codes
questions.explain: Assembly language uses short mnemonic codes (such as LDA or ADD) to represent machine operations.

questions.q: What is an advantage of writing a program in a high-level language rather than a low-level language?
options: It is easier for humans to read, write and debug
It runs without needing any translation
It is written directly in binary
It only works on one specific type of processor
questions.explain: High-level languages use English-like keywords, making them easier for people to understand, write and debug.

questions.q: Which statement about machine code is correct?
options: It is written in binary and can be executed directly by the processor
It uses mnemonics to represent instructions
It is completely machine independent
It is easier for humans to read than a high-level language
questions.explain: Machine code is the binary instruction set that the processor can execute directly without further translation.

questions.q: What does a compiler do?
options: Translates a whole high-level program into machine code before it is run
Translates and executes a program one line at a time
Converts machine code back into a high-level language
Only checks the spelling of keywords
questions.explain: A compiler translates the entire high-level source program into machine code in one go, producing an executable file.

questions.q: What does an interpreter do?
options: Translates and executes a high-level program one line at a time
Produces a complete executable file before running
Translates assembly language into a high-level language
Only runs programs already written in machine code
questions.explain: An interpreter translates and immediately executes each line of the source program in turn, stopping when it meets an error.

questions.q: How does a compiler differ from an interpreter in the way it reports errors?
options: A compiler reports all the errors together at the end after translating the whole program
A compiler stops at the very first error and cannot continue at all
An interpreter produces an executable file with an error list
An interpreter always translates the whole program before running it
questions.explain: A compiler translates the whole program and then produces a report listing all the errors found, whereas an interpreter halts at the first error it meets.

questions.q: A developer has finished a program and wants to distribute it as a standalone executable file that customers can run without the source code. Which translator should be used?
options: A compiler
An interpreter
An assembler
A device driver
questions.explain: A compiler translates the whole program into a machine-code executable that can be distributed and run without the source code or the translator.

questions.q: What does IDE stand for?
options: Integrated Development Environment
Internal Data Editor
Interactive Design Engine
Integrated Debugging Extension
questions.explain: An IDE (Integrated Development Environment) provides tools such as an editor, translator and debugger to help write and test programs.

questions.q: While testing a program in an IDE, a programmer sets a breakpoint on a line of code. What effect does this have?
options: It pauses execution at that line so variables can be inspected to help find errors
It permanently prevents the program from ever running again
It translates that line of code into binary
It highlights the keywords on that line in different colours
questions.explain: A breakpoint pauses the program at the chosen line so the programmer can examine the state of the program and locate errors.
